title: Create certification types and verify another member’s record
summary: Create a fictional Person type and record, verify another member, confirm saved holdings and type constraints, inspect unchanged policy, and compare filters with the actual HTML report.
prerequisites: Use a fictional practice department and your existing certification view, management and setup permissions.
Choose another fictional member for review; record holders cannot verify their own records.
Use Reports permission for the separate HTML report. Leave existing role requirements and global policies unchanged.

sector_examples.Chicago Fire: Separate a fictional exercise record from existing department records and use a non-holder reviewer.
sector_examples.Community care and mental health: Track operational training references without patient detail or clinical-authority claims.
sector_examples.Search and rescue: Distinguish reviewed person records from equipment records; starter templates require department review.
sector_examples.Security: Organize staff training records and their stored review status without treating a software label as authorization.
sector_examples.Wildland: Keep seasonal training references and explicit dates current; do not infer readiness from a color alone.
sector_examples.Industrial response: Keep staff records distinct from unit inspection records, using the appropriate scope and reviewer.

scenes.title: Separate records, review and self-verification
scenes.practice: Identify the pending count, then compare the holder of a record with the signed-in reviewer.

scenes.practice: Filter the gallery without selecting or adding a template, then return to the catalog.

scenes.title: Give the exercise its own type and code
scenes.practice: Prepare a unique fictional type name, code, issuer, and purpose before saving.

scenes.title: Save the verification rule and read back the type
scenes.practice: Save only your own exercise type and verify its code, twelve-month validity, and zero counts.

scenes.practice: Select the intended fictional member and new type, then inspect both date fields.

scenes.title: Enter explicit identity and dates, then save
scenes.practice: Save the explicit dates and exercise number, then check the returned pending count.

scenes.title: Verify another member and confirm persistence
scenes.practice: Review your own fictional record for another member, then confirm the stored reviewer and status.

scenes.title: Compare the person’s existing and new records
scenes.practice: Find both rows and identify the new exercise without changing the original record.

scenes.title: Check counts and the locked scope

scenes.title: Distinguish role enforcement from notifications
scenes.practice: Read the current role and notification policies, leaving every saved setting unchanged.

scenes.practice: Compare Casey’s filtered expiry with the training column in the HTML report.

scenes.title: Use a clear review process across sectors
scenes.practice: Define one appropriate fictional type and identify who should review it in your team.
